page.text:
The most important relations are those that behave like a generalized
equality. An *equivalence relation* is reflexive, symmetric, and
transitive: every element is related to itself, the relation is symmetric
between pairs, and it chains through intermediate elements. These three
laws are exactly what is needed to regard related elements as
interchangeable.
